title: Wigner's theorem for the rays of C^N: unitary or antiunitary, unique up to a phase
abstract: A machine-checked proof of Wigner's theorem for the complex projective space of C^N. Let f be any map from rays to rays that preserves the transition probability |<psi, phi>|^2 / (|psi|^2 |phi|^2). Then f is induced by a unitary or by an antiunitary (a unitary after coordinatewise complex conjugation), and in each case the inducing operator is unique up to a global phase. Nothing else is assumed about f: not linearity, not continuity, not bijectivity. The theorem is stated twice, with linear isometries (wigner, wigner_unique, wigner_unique_antiunitary) and with unitary matrices acting on rays (wigner_unitaryGroup, wigner_unitaryGroup_unique, wigner_unitaryGroup_unique_antiunitary). Mathlib, at the pinned commit, has no Wigner theorem. The proof was first completed in the author's csd-lean4 library on 2 July 2026 (commit c26c0954). Two other Lean proofs are listed under related_formalizations: one for maps on unit vectors of C^n, completed on 13 July 2026, and one whose existence theorem covers complex Hilbert spaces of any dimension, at a snapshot dated 31 October 2026. This proof is independent of both. The theorem is classical and no priority is claimed for it.
